generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The `regions` array `{"", "", "europe-west1", "europewest", "europe-west1"}` contains duplicate values (`""` appears twice, `"europe-west1"` appears twice). This looks like a leftover from iterative test development. The duplicates don't cause a failure, but they make the test's intent unclear and add no additional coverage. Consider deduplicating to `{"", "europe-west1", "europewest"}` or, if the intent was to test different normalization scenarios, use distinct values.

In the tags-based fallback, the variable `provider` is reused from the method-level declaration (which is `null` at that point since we only reach this path when `cloud.provider` was absent). While functionally correct, this is slightly confusing because the reader must track that `provider` was initially assigned from `source.get("cloud.provider")` and is now being reassigned from tag parsing. A local variable (e.g., `String tagProvider = null;`) would make the intent clearer and avoid the subtle coupling to the earlier null-check.

The new and modified test code introduces inconsistent spacing that deviates from the surrounding codebase style: `HostMetadata.fromSource (` and `Map.of (` (space before opening parenthesis), and `"cloud_provider:" + provider` (spaces around `+`). The original code in `#GA8RH` had `HostMetadata.fromSource(` and `Map.of(` without the space. Pick one convention and apply it consistently; the standard Java/Elasticsearch style is no space before `(` and no spaces around `+` in string concatenation.

review_comment:
I missed this in the last review but it is actually not required that we bump the index template version on every change. Instead, it is sufficient to bump it once per release because no cluster can observe the intermediate index template versions.

Long story short: Can you please change this value to `5` (which applies to 8.14.0) and merge the comments accordingly to include all changes that went into version `5`?

That is a good point I already thought of. My conclusion was that I do not know whether version 5 or 6 has already been deployed (locally) and used by developers. And if you don't know that, why risking to break things even if it is just one or two people?

What is the downside of increasing the version several times per release cycle?
As discussed offline, it's less risky to bump the version all the time, even if this means version jumps between releases (which are harmless) so let's stick to this convention in the future.
